title: Degree-zero reduction of canonical homotopy colimits
statement:
Use the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the complete, cocomplete model-category, weak-equivalence, cofibrant-object and Reedy terminology of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A cosimplicial resolution means a Reedy cofibrant functor $A^\bullet:\Delta\to\mathcal M$ whose structure maps are weak equivalences. Its canonical augmentation to $\operatorname{const}(A^0)$ is induced by the unique maps $[n]\to[0]$. Use homotopy colimits of [lem-coef-hocolim-reindexing-zigzags], computed by the colimit of a projectively cofibrant replacement. Let $\mathcal M$ be combinatorial, $D$ a small ordinary category, and $A:D\to\mathcal M^\Delta$ a functor whose values are cosimplicial resolutions. Put $\gamma(d)=A_d^0$ and fix $X\in\mathcal M$. For $n\geq0$, define $I_n$ to have objects $(d,u:A_d^n\to X)$ and arrows $a:d\to e$ satisfying $u'A_a^n=u$. Its value diagram $V_n:I_n\to\mathcal M$ sends $(d,u)$ to $A_d^0$, not to $A_d^n$. The collapse $[n]\to[0]$ gives $i_n:I_0\to I_n$, with $V_ni_n=V_0$. Let $K$ have objects $(d,[n],u:A_d^n\to X)$ and arrows $(a,\alpha):(d,[n],u)\to(e,[m],u')$ with $a:d\to e$, $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ and $u'A_e(\alpha)A_a^n=u$. Its value diagram is $T(d,[n],u)=A_d^n$. Degree-zero inclusion $i:I_0\to K$ induces a comparison of homotopy colimits. If $(i_n)_*:\operatorname{hocolim}_{I_0}V_0\to\operatorname{hocolim}_{I_n}V_n$ is an isomorphism in the homotopy category for every $n\geq0$, then
$$i_*:\operatorname{hocolim}_{I_0}V_0\longrightarrow\operatorname{hocolim}_K T$$
is an isomorphism there, represented by a weak-equivalence comparison of homotopy colimits. All comparisons respect the augmentation maps to $X$. No fibrancy assumption on $X$ is required.

source.place: Proposition 4.6 and its proof in Section 8, especially Proposition 8.2 and Lemma 8.1, printed pp. 186, 193-196. No Stacks tag states this canonical-homotopy-colimit result. Sources read online 2026-10-17, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Define $W:K\to\mathcal M$ by $W(d,[n],u)=A_d^0$ and $W(a,\alpha)=A_a^0$. For the unique $c_n:[n]\to[0]$, put $\eta_{(d,[n],u)}=A_d(c_n):T(d,[n],u)\to W(d,[n],u)$. Naturality is the equality $A_e(c_m)A_e(\alpha)A_a^n=A_a^0A_d(c_n)$, since $c_m\alpha=c_n$ and $A_a$ is cosimplicially natural. Every component is a weak equivalence by the resolution hypothesis, and $\eta i=1_{V_0}$. Hence [lem-coef-hocolim-reindexing-zigzags], whose constructions preserve objectwise weak equivalences, gives the isomorphism $\eta_*=H_K(\eta):\operatorname{hocolim}_K T\to\operatorname{hocolim}_K W$. Apply [lem-coef-hocolim-value-diagram-naturality] with $g=i$, $F=T$, $G=W$: its square gives $\eta_*i^T_*=i^W_*$, since $\eta i=1$. We will prove that the lower comparison $i^W_*:\operatorname{hocolim}_{I_0}V_0\to\operatorname{hocolim}_K W$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 4.6, Section 8 and Appendix A: replace the values by degree zero using the resolution augmentation; explicit agent regrouping of the same canonical diagram.

proof.text: For $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ define $\alpha^*:I_m\to I_n$ by $(d,u)\mapsto(d,uA_d(\alpha))$, and keep the arrow $a:d\to e$. The arrow condition follows from $A_e(\alpha)A_a^n=A_a^mA_d(\alpha)$. Composition of precomposition maps makes $[n]\mapsto I_n$ a strict functor $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Cat}$, and $V_n\alpha^*=V_m$ strictly. Its Cartesian Grothendieck total category over $\Delta$ is exactly $K$: a fiber arrow $(d,u)\to\alpha^*(e,u')$ is precisely an $a:d\to e$ with $u'A_e(\alpha)A_a^n=u$. Under this equality $W$ restricts to $V_n$ on each fiber and sends every transport arrow $(1_d,\alpha)$ to $1_{A_d^0}$. The transport for $c_n$ is the functor $i_n:I_0\to I_n$. These are small categories in the fixed containing universe: $D$ and $\Delta$ are small and the objects of each $I_n$ form a small union of the Hom sets $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(A_d^n,X)$. Enlarge that universe once if necessary, as allowed by the statement conventions, so all these categories remain small for both cited colimit theorems.

source.place: Section 8 proof of Proposition 4.6: explicit indexing-category version of assembling all singular degrees; the Cartesian total category and its variance are checked directly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison] to work in $\mathcal C=\mathcal M[W_{\mathcal M}^{-1}]_\infty$, writing $q$ for localization. Every small ordinary-indexed model homotopy-colimit cocone becomes its coherent colimit cocone. Use $h\mathcal C$ of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], whose morphisms are components of mapping spaces and whose composition is specified by triangles. For an ordinary category $J$, a functor $h\mathcal C\to J$ is exactly a simplicial map $\mathcal C\to N(J)$: triangles enforce composition, a path in a mapping space is a triangle with a degenerate edge and hence preserves the assigned arrow, and higher simplices of $N(J)$ are uniquely determined by their edge strings. Apply the universal property of $q$ with target $N(J)$. It identifies these functors with the functors $\mathcal M\to J$ inverting $W_{\mathcal M}$, including natural transformations. Thus $h\mathcal C$ is the ordinary localization used in the hypothesis, and the ordinary and coherent comparisons below have the same classes. The same cited node states exactly that an edge is an equivalence if and only if its component class is invertible. Thus $F_n=\operatorname{colim}_{N(I_n)}qV_n$ exists. Apply [lem-coef-cartesian-grothendieck-colimit-formula] to $B=\Delta$, $U([n])=I_n$ and $H=qW$: Step 2 verifies that transport arrows have identity images. It gives the coherent simplicial diagram $F:N(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$, whose map for $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ is $(\alpha^*)_*:F_m\to F_n$, and the equivalence $\operatorname{colim}F\simeq q\operatorname{hocolim}_K W$. Steps 4-5 below supply existence of $\operatorname{colim}F$ before the displayed equivalence is invoked; constructing $F$ requires only its fiber colimits. The fiber-inclusion clause identifies $F_0\to\operatorname{colim}F$ with the lower comparison of Step 1.

source.place: Section 8, Proposition 8.2: the total-versus-iterated homotopy-colimit comparison, expressed by the general Cartesian Grothendieck colimit formula rather than by presheaf realization.

proof.text: The unique maps $c_n:[n]\to[0]$ form a natural transformation $\mathrm{id}_{\Delta}\to\operatorname{const}([0])$: for $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ one has $c_m\alpha=c_n$. Taking opposites gives $\operatorname{const}([0])\to\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}$. Its nerve is a map $N(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^1\to N(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}}$; postcomposing with the coherent functor $F$ of Step 3 gives $s:\operatorname{const}(F_0)\to F$, including all its higher coherences. Its component is $F(c_n^{\mathrm{op}})=(i_n)_*$ by the transition formula of Step 3, and $(\alpha^*)_*s_m=s_n$ is the displayed naturality equation. The hypothesis says exactly that every $s_n$ is an equivalence, by the invertible-component criterion and localization identification established in Step 3. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences], $s$ is an equivalence of diagrams. The identity-augmented constant diagram with value $F_0$ extends to $N(\Delta_{-\infty})^{\mathrm{op}}$ by the constant functor: every object goes to $F_0$ and every simplex to its degenerate simplex. Thus it is split in the exact sense of [lem-coef-infinity-split-augmentation-colimit], whose statement makes its identity augmentation a colimit cocone, without requiring any other colimits in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.6, printed p. 196: collapse the homotopically constant simplicial homotopy colimit. Constant split augmentation supplies the colimit directly; HA 4.7.2.1-4 is the source of the cited generic theorem.

proof.text: Choose an inverse equivalence $s^{-1}:F\to\operatorname{const}(F_0)$ of the diagram equivalence in Step 4. Apply [lem-coef-colimit-cocone-transport-equivalence] with $\tau=s^{-1}$ to the colimiting identity cocone on $\operatorname{const}(F_0)$. Its precomposition gives a colimiting cocone $\mu$ on $F$ with apex $F_0$. Its degree-zero leg has the invertible class of $(s^{-1})_0$, because $s_0=1$. Thus we may take $F_0$ as $\operatorname{colim}F$, and the canonical leg $F_0\to\operatorname{colim}F$ is an equivalence. This supplies the outer colimit required in Step 3. The fiber-inclusion clause of [lem-coef-cartesian-grothendieck-colimit-formula] therefore identifies this equivalence with the lower comparison of Step 1.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.6, printed p. 196: collapse the homotopically constant simplicial homotopy colimit. Constant split augmentation supplies the colimit directly; HA 4.7.2.1-4 is the source of the cited generic theorem.

proof.text: Steps 3-5 prove that the lower arrow in the reindexing square of Step 1 is an isomorphism. Its right vertical arrow $\eta_*$ is an isomorphism, and its left vertical arrow is the identity because $\eta i=1$. Therefore $i_*:\operatorname{hocolim}_{I_0}V_0\to\operatorname{hocolim}_K T$ is an isomorphism in the homotopy category.  An actual representative can be chosen as follows. Write $Q_0V_0\to V_0$ and $Q_KT\to T$ for the projective cofibrant replacements. The restriction $i^*Q_KT\to V_0$ is a projective trivial fibration, because these are objectwise trivial fibrations. Lift $Q_0V_0\to V_0$ through it using projective cofibrancy of $Q_0V_0$. Take the colimit of the lift and compose with the ordinary reindexing cocone to obtain $\operatorname{colim}_{I_0}Q_0V_0\to\operatorname{colim}_KQ_KT$. The lift equation makes this a representative of the canonical $i_*$ and makes its composite with the evaluation augmentation to $X$ equal to the source augmentation. Apply [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] to the actual homotopy-colimit comparison representing $i_*$: its image in the ordinary localization is an isomorphism, so it is a weak equivalence. No cofibrancy or fibrancy of its endpoints is required by that node. Finally the original $T$-cocone has component $u:A_d^n\to X$, since an arrow of $K$ satisfies exactly $u'T(a,\alpha)=u$. Restricting it along $i$ gives $u:A_d^0\to X$, the $V_0$-augmentation. Thus the original comparison commutes with the augmentations, before passing to the homotopy category; the auxiliary $W$ need not have a strict augmentation to $X$. For a fixed $n$, choose the last-vertex map $v_n:[0]\to[n]$. The $V_n$-augmentation has component $uA_d(v_n)$; it is natural in $I_n$ by naturality of $A_a$. On the image of $i_n$ this is $u_0A_d(c_n)A_d(v_n)=u_0$, because $c_nv_n=1_{[0]}$. Thus each assumed degree comparison also respects its augmentation to $X$. No step used fibrancy of $X$.

source.place: Conclusion of Proposition 4.6, printed p. 196; augmentation compatibility checked from the actual original cocones, not from a putative strict augmentation of W.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 4.6, Section 8: explicit alternative regrouping proof using the resolution augmentation and Cartesian Grothendieck colimit formula; no bisimplicial-set result is applied to arbitrary model-category objects.
